answer: Bounded-continent residency permits: each identity must carry a device that continuously proves it sits inside a fixed physical region (a cedar reserve's perimeter) using attested location plus periodic challenge signals. A juniper grove acts as a second zone, and only addresses resident in one named oasis cluster can transact. An operator cannot rent thousands of co-located devices without each showing independent, confirmed coordinates, so the per-identity cost is purchasing or maintaining distinct physical hosts at verifiable spots.
